ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening of all directors, shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners against the Gibraltar Sanctions List, UK HMT Consolidated List, United Nations Security Council Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List and EU consolidated sanctions (to the extent domestically implemented). Enhanced due diligence is required for any politically exposed person (PEP) or high-risk jurisdiction. Screening must be performed at pre-incorporation and on a continuous basis through the registered agent.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies Registry Gibraltar (operated by the Registrar of Companies, Government of Gibraltar)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin characters. The name may be in English or any language transliterated into the Latin alphabet. The Registrar requires a statutory standard exact translation or transcription where the name is not in English. Mandatory suffix indicating limited liability ('Limited' or 'Ltd') is required.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may submit a written request for reconsideration within 14 days to the Registrar of Companies, stating why the name should be accepted. Amendments may also be proposed. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, an appeal may be lodged to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar by way of judicial review within 28 days of the final decision. A new name application without prejudice may be filed at any point.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as a substitute for the statutory registered office. The company must maintain a physical registered office in Gibraltar. A virtual commercial address may be used for correspondence only in addition to the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated 3% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection for a low-risk standard commodity trading entity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Her Majesty's Government of Gibraltar – Income Tax Office (ITO); portal: https://www.tax.gov.gi
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-Gibraltar incorporated entity (Bermuda Exempted Company) establishing a taxable presence in Gibraltar must: (1) register with the Income Tax Office for a Gibraltar Income Tax reference number (TIN) via the online agent portal or Form GIP001; (2) if central management and control will be exercised in Gibraltar, elect or notify tax residence accordingly; (3) file certified constitutional documents, board resolutions, register of directors and shareholders, and evidence of a Gibraltar service address or registered office; (4) appoint a Gibraltar-resident authorized agent or material person to submit filings; (5) for goods movements, apply to the Gibraltar Customs & Excise Department for an EORI number; (6) for VAT purposes, no Gibraltar VAT registration exists, but any non-established business is still required to appoint a fiscal representative solely for customs and duty purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' election. Foreign companies may be treated as tax-resident where central management and control is exercised in Gibraltar. Elections are available for group relief (joint taxation of Gibraltarian group companies), capital allowances pooling, and special purpose vehicles electing to be treated as entities subject to the territorial Income Tax Act. Hybrid mismatch restriction rules under the Taxation (Hybrids) Act, implementing EU ATAD, limit the effectiveness of any transparent/tax-exempt classification from the Bermuda parent structure.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST in Gibraltar; indirect fiscal controls are applied through import duty, excise duty, and customs rules
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable – Gibraltar does not levy VAT/GST. For customs purposes, all businesses conducting import, export, or transit of physical goods across Gibraltar's frontiers must hold an Economic Operator Registration and Identification (EORI) number; no minimum turnover threshold is required for EORI registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar does not mandate real-time fiscal e-invoicing, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC). Customs declarations are submitted electronically using the Single Administrative Document (SAD) system. No API-based real-time clearance platform or mandatory third-party e-invoicing network is in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable – Gibraltar does not operate a VAT/GST system. Consequently there is no export VAT zero-rating claim mechanism, no output VAT at 0%, and no input VAT refund entitlement. Exports of raw cane sugar from Gibraltar's customs territory are outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect taxation; duty and excise may only arise on import into the final destination market.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document – SAD)
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) evidencing collection of export proceeds
Certificate of Origin and any preferential proof of origin claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT clawback applies in Gibraltar given the absence of a VAT system. Fraudulent customs declarations, misdescription of sugar polarization or HS tariff classification, false claims for customs duty relief or excise suspensive arrangements, and improper use of inward processing rules attract penalties of up to 150% of the duty evaded, seizure and forfeiture of the goods, monetary fines, and criminal liability including imprisonment of up to 7 years. Retrospective assessments may be raised within 5 years of the export date, with unlimited clawback in cases of fraud, together with director disqualification orders and withdrawal of the EORI registration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (London) - de facto monetary authority anchoring the Gibraltar pound through the statutory 1:1 GIP/GBP currency-board peg; the Government of Gibraltar issues GIP notes under the Currency Notes Act; Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) - licensing and prudential supervisor of Gibraltar banks under the Financial Services Act 2019; Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA) - home-jurisdiction regulator of the Bermuda Exempted Company, with no exchange-control permit regime applicable to exempted companies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full unrestricted convertibility on both current and capital account. Gibraltar repealed the Exchange Control Act 1972 in 1979 in line with the United Kingdom; no prior permission is required for inward or outward remittances, dividends, loan repayments, or trade settlements. Bermuda imposes no exchange controls on Exempted Companies, and the United Kingdom maintains a free cross-border capital regime. The US dollar, being the operative settlement currency of the VHP raw cane sugar trade, is freely convertible in London and Gibraltar wholesale markets. Profit-remittance hurdles are documentary only: CRS/FATCA self-certification, Bermuda economic-substance reporting, and the bank's source-of-funds clearance for each dividend or distribution. Zero statutory withholding taxes apply on dividends, interest, royalties, or management fees in Bermuda and Gibraltar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (annual confirmation of registered particulars, share capital, members and directors)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of incorporation (the annual return date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties escalate from GBP 50 to GBP 500; continued non-compliance can trigger prosecution and administrative strike-off after the Registrar issues a notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and auditor's report (if not audit-exempt)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 9 months after the financial year-end (private company); 6 months for public companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties scale with each month of delay, from GBP 100 up to GBP 1,000; accounts outstanding for 12+ months subject the company to compulsory strike-off and director disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Tax Return (income tax self-assessment declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office / Commissioner of Income Tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 November following the tax year of assessment, unless the Commissioner grants an extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest accrues on unpaid tax; penalties up to 100% of the tax due, daily default fines, and possible enforcement seizure or strike-off for prolonged failure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Economic Substance Return (required if the company performs a relevant activity such as distribution and service centre operations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office / Registrar of Companies (beneficial ownership portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the financial year (in practice aligned with the tax return deadline)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance can attract fines up to GBP 10,000 per offence and may be sanctioned by administrative restoration action, including strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit is compulsory unless the company qualifies as small under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, meeting at least two of: (i) annual turnover not exceeding GBP 1,000,000; (ii) balance sheet total not exceeding GBP 500,000; (iii) average number of employees not exceeding 10. Companies that are public, regulated financial services entities, or members of a non-small group are never exempt from audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted for use in Gibraltar; small and medium entities may alternatively apply UK GAAP (FRS 102) as Gibraltar GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The beneficial ownership register must be filed annually via the Gibraltar Beneficial Ownership Secure Search (BOSS) system at the Registrar of Companies. Annual confirmation is due by the anniversary of the annual return date, and any shareholding transfer, director change, or significant control change must be reported within 28 days. The registered agent is responsible for keeping the statutory registers updated and lodged at the registered office.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% — Gibraltar Corporate Income Tax (CIT) for Large Business Units (LBUs) from fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2025; Bermuda Exempted Companies remain subject to a 0% Bermuda CIT rate unless caught by the Bermuda Corporate Income Tax Act 2023 domestic top-up tax (15%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
